meaning.evidence: A Cartesian space-time jet collects a field and all its Cartesian space-time derivatives through the stated order.

notation.evidence: Equation (5.23) writes |.|_m for the largest absolute value among the field and those derivatives through order m.

prerequisites.evidence: The field, derivatives, order cutoff, and maximum absolute value are all stated before |.|_m is used later.

proof_job.evidence: The jet is the size used for normalized-coefficient estimates while residual identities are written with physical fields.

target.exact_quote:
The residual identities below use physical fields, while their estimates use normalized
coefficients. A Cartesian space--time jet collects a field and all its Cartesian space--time
derivatives up to the stated order. Equation~\eqref{eq:5.23} writes
\NSi{NS-F-P101-008}{|\cdot|_m} for the largest absolute value among them through that order.

source_locator.exact_text:
We use physical fields in residual identities and normalized coefficients in the estimates below. The
Cartesian space--time jet notation \NSi{NS-F-P101-008}{|\cdot|_m} is defined in \eqref{eq:5.23}.

meaning.evidence: Longitudinal means measured in the direction of the phase normal.

notation.evidence: Equation (7.39) estimates the scalar product of the full amplitude a_m with that normal, after the curl correction r_m is included.

prerequisites.evidence: The phase normal, full amplitude, transverse input, curl correction, and their coefficient classes are identified first.

proof_job.evidence: The distinction matters because the full divergence-free velocity is the advecting factor in quadratic transport.

target.exact_quote:
Here \NSi{NS-F-P101-017}{r_m} is the correction created by taking the curl. If
\NSi{NS-F-P101-018}{t_m\in \mathsf W_\alpha}, then Lemma~\ref{lem:7.7} gives
\NSi{NS-F-P101-019}{r_m\in \mathsf W_{\alpha+1/2-\kappa_s}}. Here longitudinal means measured in
the direction of the phase normal. Equation~\eqref{eq:7.39} estimates the scalar product with that normal for the
full amplitude \NSi{NS-F-P101-020}{a_m}. This difference matters
in the quadratic transport term, because the factor doing the advecting is the full divergence-free
velocity.

source_locator.exact_text:
Here \NSi{NS-F-P101-017}{r_m} is the curl correction. If
\NSi{NS-F-P101-018}{t_m\in \mathsf W_\alpha}, then Lemma~\ref{lem:7.7} gives
\NSi{NS-F-P101-019}{r_m\in \mathsf W_{\alpha+1/2-\kappa_s}}. The longitudinal estimate \eqref{eq:7.39}
applies to the complete amplitude \NSi{NS-F-P101-020}{a_m}. This distinction matters in quadratic
transport: its advecting factor is the complete divergence-free velocity.
